Here, we discuss our individual patient's problems through series of inputs from an available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence-based inputs. This E-logbook also reflects my patient-centered online portfolio and your valuable inputs on the comments are welcome."},"link":[{"rel":"http://schemas.google.com/g/2005#feed","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/nikhilasampathkumar.blogspot.com\/feeds\/posts\/default"},{"rel":"self","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/12123993088122961\/posts\/default?alt=json\u0026max-results=3"},{"rel":"alternate","type":"text/html","href":"https:\/\/nikhilasampathkumar.blogspot.com\/"},{"rel":"hub","href":"http://pubsubhubbub.appspot.com/"},{"rel":"next","type":"application/atom+xml","href":"https:\/\/www.blogger.com\/feeds\/12123993088122961\/posts\/default?alt=json\u0026start-index=4\u0026max-results=3"}],"author":[{"name":{"$t":"Nikhila Sampath Kumar"},"uri":{"$t":"http:\/\/www.blogger.com\/profile\/06436559575321884061"},"email":{"$t":"noreply@blogger.com"},"gd$image":{"rel":"http://schemas.google.com/g/2005#thumbnail","width":"16","height":"16","src":"https:\/\/img1.blogblog.com\/img\/b16-rounded.gif"}}],"generator":{"version":"7.00","uri":"http://www.blogger.com","$t":"Blogger"},"openSearch$totalResults":{"$t":"14"},"openSearch$startIndex":{"$t":"1"},"openSearch$itemsPerPage":{"$t":"3"},"entry":[{"id":{"$t":"tag:blogger.com,1999:blog-12123993088122961.post-269124914847398128"},"published":{"$t":"2023-08-10T00:45:00.019-07:00"},"updated":{"$t":"2023-08-10T03:03:19.272-07:00"},"title":{"type":"text","$t":"38y F with inability to open her mouth, dysphagia since 2 months, pancytopenia and parapharyngeal abscess"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003EIntroduction: This is an online E-log Entry Blog to discuss, understand and review the clinical scenarios and data analysis of patients so as to develop my clinical competency in comprehending clinical cases, and providing evidence-based inputs.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENote: The cases have been shared after taking consent from the patient\/guardian. All names and other identifiers have been removed to secure and respect the privacy of the patient and the family.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EConsent: An informed consent has been taken from the patient in the presence of the family attenders and other witnesses as well and the document has been conserved securely for future references.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA 38-year-old female presented with the chief complaints of difficulty in opening her mouth and left ear pain since 2 months, and difficulty in swallowing since 1 month.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of Presenting Illness:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESequence of events:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E12th June, 2023: The patient had her left lower 2nd molar extracted for caries which was causing a toothache.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E16th June, 2023: She first experienced difficulty in opening her mouth coupled with severe pain (she rated the pain as 9\/10). Both of these symptoms were insidious in onset and have been progressing since then.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E17th June, 2023: She was taken to local dental hospital where forceful opening of her mouth caused left ear pain which radiated to the left side of her neck.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe used some unknown painkiller injections prescribed by a local RMP during this time. Her pain responded to these injections but aggravated on prolonging the interval between them. She took a total of 4 of these injections.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3rd week of June: She visited one other hospital, where she was referred ti an ENT specialist for further examination. No treatment was prescribed here and patient did not take any new medications.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EJuly, 2023: She started having difficulty and pain while swallowing both solids and liquids.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe also started experiencing shortness of breath (Grade II NYHA) which was relieved on rest.\u003Cbr \/\u003ENo orthopnea, PND, chest pain or palpitations. No blood in stools, hematuria or menorrhagia.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EJuly 26th, 2023: Low grade fever that was insidious in onset, non progressive, assosciated with chills and rigors. Lasted for 3 days. Relieved on medication (paracetamol).\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAugust 2023: The patient arrived at the local dental hospital for further relief from her symptoms but was referred to the medicine department in view of pancytopenia.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E8\/8\/23: A referral by the department of ENT was done on 8\/8\/23.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFindings: Mild anterior DNS to the left, grade III trismus, ulcerated left lateral pharyngeal wall.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAdvice: Patient was referred to OMFS, asked to get Xray of head and neck in AP and lateral views and an MRI.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E9\/8\/23: A referral by the department of Oral and Maxillofacial surgery was done on 9\/8\/23.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFindings: Dental fluorosis, TMJ dysfunction with decreased mouth opening (2 fingers breadth) , dental caries.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESuspicion of parapharyngeal abscess (?)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAdvice: physiotherapy (mouth opening exercises) , VOVERAN and FLEXON MR.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient asked to return to the dental OPD in 5 days for review.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of past illness:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot a known case of HTN, DM, Asthma, TB, Epilepsy, CAD, CVD\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMedication History:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUses homeopathic medications for headaches, used unknown analgesic injections during the course of her treatment outside the hospital.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPersonal history:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDecreased appetite, diet has mostly been soft and liquid.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBowel movements: 1\/day, normal in consistency.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUrine output: 2-3\/day, no burning on micturition.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EModerate drinker, drinks 1 glass of toddy once every 10 days. She has been drinking for the past 6 years.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe does not smoke, chew tobacco\/gutkha\/pan masala. No other addictions\/substance abuse.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFood and drug allergies: No known allergies.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMenstrual and obstetric history:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMenarche: 12yrs of age\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECycle: 5\/30, normal flow, regular.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAge at marriage: 19 years.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo children.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDaily routine:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPrior routine:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAgricultural labourer by occupation who lives with her husband. She works on roughly 4 out of 7 days a week. She wakes up at 5am, starts her day by cleaning her house and yard, cooking meals and drinks a cup of chai at 6am with her husband. She has her first meal at 8am and leaves to work at 9am on foot. The field she works in is roughly half a kilometre away from where she lives. Here she spends most of her time either sowing seeds, husking grain or weeding. She takes a 30 minute nap near the field itself at 1pm, wakes up and has lunch at 2pm. She goes back home between 5-6pm and cooks dinner. She has dinner between 7-8pm and goes to bed between 9-9:30pm. She considers her physical activity levels as moderate (described by her as not too much but not too little either).\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERoutine since the onset of her illness:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe has not been going to work. She has had a severe loss of appetite and some sleep disturbance. She wakes up at 6:30am, cooks and cleans her house. She has not been having solid food for the past 1.5-2months. For breakfast she tries to eat soft foods like mashed khichdi or powdered idlis, and drinks 2 glasses of jowar water at roughly 3pm and 8pm. She goes to bed at 9pm.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFamily History\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo similar complaints in her family.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGeneral physical Exam:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn admission:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EVitals:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAfebrile (101.2F)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBP: 100\/70mmHg\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHR: 80bpm\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERR: 20cpm\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESpO2: 97% on RA\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGRBS: 90mg\/dL\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; year old male with episodic cough"},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;Introduction: This is an online E-log Entry Blog to discuss, understand and review the clinical scenarios and data analysis of patients so as to develop my clinical competency in comprehending clinical cases, and providing evidence-based inputs.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENote: The cases have been shared after taking consent from the patient\/guardian. All names and other identifiers have been removed to secure and respect the privacy of the patient and the family.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EConsent: An informed consent has been taken from the patient in the presence of the family attenders and other witnesses as well and the document has been conserved securely for future references.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;A 35-year-old male presented with the chief complaints of episodic dry cough and noisy breathing since 7 months.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of Presenting Illness:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient was apparently asymptomatic 7 months ago when he first noticed a dry hacking cough and noisy breathing that was insidious in onset and gradually progressed to his current frequency.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe first went to a local physician who prescribed him a 1 week course of antibiotics. On noting no improvement, he went to a physician again who prescribed him a second week long course of antibiotics. This is his third visit for his ailment. The patient has had no previous imaging done.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe cough is aggravated by several factors:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Col style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cli\u003ECold weather\/ AC rooms\/ cold breeze hitting his face\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003EExertion (when asked about the type of activity, he says riding his bike in the summer months or brisk walking to work makes it worse)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/li\u003E\u003Cli\u003ELying down\/sleeping: he complains of severe cough and noisy breathing when he lies down to go to bed, to the extent where he cannot sleep and needs to sit upright or take a walk. He says taking a walk decreases his cough in such instances.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ol\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E24\/7\/23: The patient couldn't sleep all night because of his cough.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EProlonged coughing leads to chest pain and shortness of breath in his case.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient complains of increased fatigue and weakness in the past 6-7 months. He says he has not had any weight changes as all his clothes fit him the same. He has had no changes in appetite.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of past illness:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EK\/C\/O Hypertension since 2 years.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EComplains of occasional dry eyes at the end of the day.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENot a known case of DM, Asthma, TB, Epilepsy, CAD, CVD\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMedication History:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHe was prescribed this antihypertensive 2 years ago and has been taking it ever since.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEjxsw07GeR7841QlfKmR2prw5yBMVUL9HBW6Sbdz8QkVRCnMYoAawtYsPnipaGNuFd78fNojJIgSOiRXB4QNQ6z-inpMG9bm6E_r_AoybBN121rv-DbA8QE00zwIIc2XsVXx2ZeR-cOeb0FF1vYUb7qVq9B-3ftwD3XDAUsBDeAHbDYIcDYo8_BB4eCNT8\/s4000\/IMG-20230725-WA0000.jpeg\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"4000\" data-original-width=\"2250\" height=\"320\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEjxsw07GeR7841QlfKmR2prw5yBMVUL9HBW6Sbdz8QkVRCnMYoAawtYsPnipaGNuFd78fNojJIgSOiRXB4QNQ6z-inpMG9bm6E_r_AoybBN121rv-DbA8QE00zwIIc2XsVXx2ZeR-cOeb0FF1vYUb7qVq9B-3ftwD3XDAUsBDeAHbDYIcDYo8_BB4eCNT8\/s320\/IMG-20230725-WA0000.jpeg\" width=\"180\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient took 2 full courses of an unknown antibiotic 3 months ago.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESurgical history:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo surgical history\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPersonal history:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENormal appetite, mixed diet\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBowel movements: 1\/day, normal in consistency.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUrine output: 2-3\/day, no burning on micturition.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOccasional drinker, drinks 90ml of hard liquor once every 3-4 months.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESmokes 1-2 cigarettes\/ month. He claims that his smoking has no effect on his cough and does not worsen it.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHas been chewing 1 packet of ghutka a day for the past 5 years.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFood and drug allergies: No known allergies.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDaily routine:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient lives with his wife, child, his mother and his two sisters. He is a software engineer and works close to home.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient's record: He wakes up at 7:50 and has a cup of tea before leaving to work at 9. He states that he has his first meal at 11am. He resumes work and takes his next break at 3pm, which is when he goes back home to take a shower. This is followed by his second meal at home. He goes back to work at around 5pm and stays there until 10pm. He has dinner between 11pm and 12am and goes to bed at 1am.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EWife and sister's account: He wakes up right before leaving to work, sometimes at 8. His daily schedule is very irregular, with his first meal being as late as 3pm sometimes. His sister claims that on some days he brushes his teeth at 11am and takes a bath at night. He has 2 meals on more days than he has 3.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn asking the patient to rate his level of day to day physical activity on a scale of 0-10, with 0 being no activity at all and 10 being athletic, the patient gave himself a 1.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFamily History\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo similar complaints in her family.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHis father was diagnosed with tuberculosis 5 years ago for which he received treatment and was treatment success was confirmed that following year. His father passed away due to complications of covid infection in 2020. He was diabetic.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EThe patient's wife has had chest pain for the past 6 months and complains of increasing abdominal distension since her C- section in 2021. cases have been shared after taking consent from the patient\/guardian. All names and other identifiers have been removed to secure and respect the privacy of the patient and the family.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EConsent: An informed consent has been taken from the patient in the presence of the family attenders and other witnesses as well and the document has been conserved securely for future references.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u0026nbsp;A 80-year-old female presented with the chief complaints of discharge from the perianal region since 15 days\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EHistory of Presenting Illness:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1\/7\/23: The patient was apparently asymptomatic before 1\/7\/23 when she developed a swelling that was a size of a coin in her perianal region which was initially not associated with any pain or fever. Her daughter reports seeing the swelling on the first day of the patient's complaint and said it did not appear inflamed and it was not assosciated with discharge.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4\/7\/23: The patient reported sudden and severe pain in her pelvic and perianal region that woke her up in the morning. The pain was of a dull aching type, intermittent, non radiating and with no aggravating factors. She reports no history of trauma to the region. She also had a fever and complained of her legs aching till her knees that day.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;She was given an unknown medication on this day that relieved her pain and fever temporarily. The patient continued using this medication intermittently in the following days to relieve her symptoms. The patient only ate one small meal on this day as she had loss of appetite.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5\/7\/23: The patient noted some discharge from the perianal region which was initially scant and non bloody.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6\/7\/23: Her symptoms persisted, with an increase in the intensity of pain in perianal region. Her daughter noticed soiling of her clothes and the foul smelling discharge. The patient started complaining of burning micturition\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E12\/7\/23: Patient started complaining of throat pain and difficulty swallowing (solids \u0026gt;liquids)\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; She was in severe pain and was shouting. The abscess was drained by General surgery and a dressing with hydrogen peroxide, betadine and NS was placed. The patient was also given neomol for the pain.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E17\/7\/23: A psychiatry referral was done to investigate her history of psychosis and paranoia. She was prescribed Olanzapine 25mg once a day and lorazepam as needed for irritability and disturbed sleep.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EA pulmonology referral was also done in view of her productive cough that worsened in the past 15 days. She was prescribed ascoril syrup and an appetite stimulant. Sputum tests for AFB and CBNAAT were advised.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E...\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHistory of past illness:\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EStrabismus of right eye since birth.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe was diagnosed with hypertension 10 years ago which she manages with Atenolol 50mg, twice a day. It was an incidental diagnosis made when she visited a local RMP for a fever.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of minor head injury without any loss of consciousness, nausea, vomiting, blurring of vision 5 years ago; it was treated with 3 stitches for a laceration.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe was diagnosed with Chronic Kidney disease in February, 2023 that is being managed conservatively.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe has a history of psychosis that first occurred in February, 2023 that was managed with risperidone and clozapine 25mg for 2 months.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003EMedication History:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EUses an unknown syrup for her intermittent cough.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003ESurgical history:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ECataract surgery of the right eye 12 years ago and left eye 8 years ago.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPersonal history:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #3e3f3c; font-family: Lora, serif; font-size: 20px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EShe has decreased appetite and dysphagia, eats 1 small meal a day.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #3e3f3c; font-family: Lora, serif; font-size: 20px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EBowel movements: 1\/day, normal in consistency. Patient reports pain with stooling on the first two days after the onset of her symptoms.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #3e3f3c; font-family: Lora, serif; font-size: 20px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EUrine output: 2-3\/day, burning on micturition.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #3e3f3c; font-family: Lora, serif; font-size: 20px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EQuit drinking toddy and chewing tobacco 20 years ago. No other drug use.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"background-color: white; color: #3e3f3c; font-family: Lora, serif; font-size: 20px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: georgia; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EFood and drug allergies: No known allergies.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: medium;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDaily routine:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe lives by herself. Before the onset of her illness she used to wake up at 4am. She spent her time until 9am cooking, cleaning and doing her laundry.\u0026nbsp; At 9am she usually ate one small meal. Her next meal was at 2pm after which she used to take a 1-2 hour nap. Her next two meals were at 5pm and 7pm. She has always had small meals that her family attributes to her getting older. She occasionally had a glass of milk before going to bed at 9 or 10pm.\u003Cbr \/\u003EShe went to live with her daughter 2 weeks before the onset of her symptoms.
